messages:
alice: Hey team, we've got a customer on Safari 16 hitting intermittent SSE disconnects and partial event payloads. They say reconnects sometimes come back with a 401 and other times the stream just stalls. Started after we put the endpoint behind the new CDN config yesterday.
ben: ugh. any logs from the user or a repro URL?
alice: They provided an edge URL and a screenshot of Network tab showing a 304 on follow-up requests and then no more events after that. Also their server logs show the client getting a 304 from the CDN when doing an If-None-Match on the SSE endpoint.
ben: 304 on an SSE endpoint = red flag. SSE should never be cached. Did we set Cache-Control on that path?
alice: We had a generic caching policy at the edge that respects origin headers, origin had ETag. Looks like the edge decided to honor it for that path.
carmela: Confirming Safari has some weirdness when an EventSource receives non-chunked or cached response types. Also Safari's reconnect sometimes uses a different internal request mechanism that won't include Authorization headers the browser doesn't automatically attach. If the CDN responds with 304 the browser might treat it as no new bytes, causing the polyfill/reconnect logic to stall.
oliver: Do we have the exact request/response traces? Can the customer run a curl repro?
alice: I asked for curl output, they sent this minimal repro command they used to compare origin vs edge:
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer CUSTOMER_TOKEN" "https://edge.customer.example/sse/stream"
```
And edge returned:
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Date: Tue, 03 Jan 2026 14:10:20 GMT
Server: fast-cdn
Connection: keep-alive
ETag: "abc123"
```
Then browser logs show: "EventSource: connection closed" and no reconnect Authorization header in the subsequent request (per their devtools capture).
ben: Standard EventSource doesn't support custom headers, so many polyfills emulate with XHR/fetch. If the polyfill's reconnect does a conditional GET (If-None-Match) and the edge returns 304, XHR may close the body and the SSE parser doesn't resume.
cdn-bot: Edge rule id 550 matched path /sse/* with caching ttl 300. Origin returned ETag; caching applied.
carmela: Immediate mitigation: set origin headers for SSE endpoints to prevent caching. Recommended headers: `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` OR `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Connection: keep-alive` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Also add `Vary: Authorization` so CDN won't serve cached responses for different auth tokens.
ben: Also we should ensure the CDN is configured to not compress/chunk-transform SSE endpoints (no-transform).
alice: I put suggested headers into a quick-check snippet for them to test on origin:
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, no-transform
Connection: keep-alive
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://customer.app
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Authorization
```
They tried with these and said the 304s stopped and Safari resumed receiving continuous events for a while, but then reported a 401 on a reconnect attempt after ~110s.
oliver: 401 on reconnect = token not forwarded on reconnect. EventSource (native) won't include auth header unless it's a cookie or the resource is on same origin with credentials. If they rely on Authorization header, the polyfill might set it on the first request but not on the automatic reconnect (or the CDN could be stripping Authorization on certain retried paths).
ben: Two prongs: (1) ensure CDN forwards Authorization to origin and doesn't cache responses with Authorization unless Vary: Authorization, (2) recommend token location alternatives. Query-string tokens work but are less secure. Best is cookie with SameSite=None + secure for browser flows so native EventSource sends it automatically.
carmela: Also verify the EventSource polyfill used by the customer. Some polyfills set `withCredentials` for XHR; if not set, cookies won't be sent on reconnect. Polyfill examples (node-eventsource or eventsource-polyfill) differ. Ask them to paste which one they use, or switch to native EventSource if possible now that caching is fixed.
alice: Customer uses `eventsource-polyfill` in their frontend bundle. I asked them to inspect the polyfill's codepath for reconnect: do they re-attach headers/cookies? They replied that reconnection uses a plain GET without headers in their build.
ben: For immediate band-aid we can recommend adding `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and moving auth to cookie so native EventSource behavior works, or update the polyfill to persist the Authorization token across reconnects.
carmela: Long-term, we should make the SSE endpoint in our docs explicit: "Do not cache SSE endpoints. Set Vary: Authorization if using token auth. Prefer cookie-based auth for browser SSE or use WebSocket for authenticated streams. If using CDN, set a no-cache rule for /sse/ or bypass the cache entirely." Link: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events
deploy-bot: Action created: SUPPORT-4492 - "Investigate Safari SSE disconnects - edge caching + auth" assigned to cdn-team, priority P1, due 2026-01-07.
alice: I've asked the customer for a HAR file. Also asked them to try a quick repro using curl directly to origin (bypassing edge) and to run Node-based SSE client to compare.
oliver: Quick repro commands to recommend to them:
1) Direct to origin (bypass CDN):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" "https://origin.customer.example/sse/stream"
```
2) Edge (shows caching behavior):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" "https://edge.customer.example/sse/stream"
```
3) Use node to emulate polyfill (xhr-style):
```
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://edge.customer.example/sse/stream');
es.on('message', e => console.log('msg', e.data));
```
Note: real node eventsource libs often allow headers: `{ headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } }`.
ben: Suggested fixes for customer (ordered):
- Set `Cache-Control: no-store` or `no-cache, no-transform` on SSE responses.
- Add `Vary: Authorization` on origin to stop CDN serving cached responses across tokens.
- Ensure CDN rule excludes /sse/* from caching or respects origin `Cache-Control` for that path.
- If using token header auth, either switch to secure cookie auth for browser clients or ensure the polyfill persists headers on reconnect.
- As a fallback consider WebSockets for authenticated bidirectional streams.
alice: I'll draft a short KB for Support with the above and sample header snippets and curl commands. Assigning follow-ups: cdn-team to update edge rule (cdn-team), frontend-eng to produce polyfill checklist (ben), and customer success to confirm token strategy with customer (carmela).
cdn-bot: Edge rule 550 updated: TTL removed for /sse/*, passthrough enabled.
alice: Customer confirmed after removing caching and ensuring cookie auth the disconnects stopped in their last 30m test. They still want a doc we can link to. I'll write up the KB and paste in this thread when ready.
ben: Nice. Also add a note about Safari-specific quirks: prefer native EventSource when possible and avoid conditional GETs (If-None-Match) on SSE endpoints.
alice: Thanks all — marking initial triage done. Will follow up with KB and the HAR attached once we get it. :thumbsup:
